As you may be aware coffee is primarily sold on this planet/colony as :

  • 'Expressso' (all variants)
  • Instant (all variants)
  • Percolated (all variants) (with correct coffee)

i'd like to go though my common sense discoveries and why one appears to be so much superior in many vectors - i'd like to thank my human brother for helping me make these discoveries.

Expresso

http://2.bp.blogspot.com/-YjzansbVhKs/VGgO9CvV4CI/AAAAAAAAADA/Kqm1n0tN_zQ/s1600/Espresso-coffee-machine%2BMAXIMA%2BXL.jpg

is by far and away the most popular in some nations on Earth.

The key to understanding Expresso is to understand pressure cooking basically the water is put under pressure to both raise the temp and pass though the beans to 'instantly' release the coffee.

however i'd more liken it to the difference between say microwaving a potato leaving it still slightly undercooked and slow cooking a potato.

When pulling apart an 'expresso' device you will discover many aspects of the way the coffee is released from the presumably roasted bean.

  • Often the pipes that carry high pressure heated water are plastic. (even in some so called premium brands)
  • Often the insides of the machinery are a perfect temp and moister for various small insects to live.

Expresso is primarily what is served in European / Australian branded outlets and other places.

Instant

So called instant coffee is a processed product that is often used in homes and businesses this is usually just poured into a cup and then boiled water is poured onto the powder thus causing a type of 'instant' peculation of the coffee.

The problems with 'Instant' coffee is you have to trust whomever processed the coffee. in most cases that will be a corporation you know next to nothing about , and they do not have to under many 'laws' (rules and regulations) disclose the process by which the coffee was made 'instant'

Percolated

The first time i tried actually percolated Coffee i knew i would never drink coffee any other way.

the process is very simple and is much more likened to 'Slow cooking' the coffee as opposed to trying to (half) pressure cook it which you will note gives 'Expresso' it's distinct bitter flavor.

here is an example of a Coffee Peculator :

https://i.pinimg.com/736x/65/01/8d/65018de9bf4aace6d70c715e553dc1ff.jpg

How does this magic work?

https://i.imgur.com/uGS6Tfp.png

you see the hot water is simply transfered to the top section where the ground coffee is placed it is then gravity fed down though the coffee and out though the 'filter' - it's important to note that the 'filter' is just a series of small punctured holes in a stainless steel plate.

if you are a lover of coffee (as i am) i implore you to try this simple and cheap method of making coffee.

a Peculator typically sells for just a little over the price of a normal boil jug but you may struggle to find them in some 'nations' fortunately my brother sent me mine from Sweden. however i'm certain you can buy such an item online. however as it is just stainless steel you could probably fashion one out of a stainless steel jug / pot if you are so creatively inclined.

I use a standard household coffee grinder to then grind up some coffee (this solves mostly the 'unknowable' aspect related to 'instant' coffee) i then scope some into the upper chamber - I also have been experimenting with adding a pinch of Turmeric and at tiny pinch of pink Himalayan salt, both these in small quantities add no discernible flavor and the salt seems to add an extra smoothness, you will know if you added too much of either.

and although it sounds difficult this is definitely the simplest way i have ever made coffee as one jug makes about 8~ cups you can pre grind coffee and keep in a jar - so it's just a matter of filling the peculator with (presumably clean) water and scooping about 4 or 5 scoops into the upper chamber and hitting the 'go' button.
